title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This typed page (numbered 30) does not belong to the motives/Deuring-orders material on the surrounding manuscript pages. It is the end of a proof of the Frobenius integrability theorem, in non-homogeneous (Pfaffian system) form, for holomorphic or analytic data. It appears to come from a draft course or treatise on analytic functions.

Setting. We are given functions U_{ij}(x;y), with x in C^p (or R^p) and y in C^q, satisfying the integrability conditions (24):
∂U_{ij}/∂x_k + Σ_h (∂U_{ij}/∂y_h) U_{kh} = ∂U_{kj}/∂x_i + Σ_h (∂U_{kj}/∂y_h) U_{ih}.
We want a local solution u(x) of the system ∂u_j/∂x_i = U_{ij}(x;u(x)) with u(x_0)=y_0.

Method (radial integration).
1. Let v(t)=v(t;x_0,x,y_0) be the solution of the ODE (26), dv/dt = U(x_0+t(x−x_0); v)·(x−x_0), with v(0)=y_0. It is defined for |t|<2.
2. Differentiating (26) with respect to x_k gives an equation for ∂v_j/∂x_k.
3. The page computes d/dt of t·U_{kj}(x_0+t(x−x_0); v(t)) by the chain rule.
4. Using (24), the differences w_{kj} = ∂v_j/∂x_k − t·U_{kj}(…) satisfy the linear homogeneous system (27): dw_{kj}/dt = Σ_{i,h} (x_i−x_{i0}) (∂U_{ij}/∂y_h) w_{kh}.
5. Since w(0)=0, uniqueness gives w ≡ 0. At t=1 this says that u(x) := v(1;x_0,x,y_0) satisfies ∂u_j/∂x_i = U_{ij}(x;u).
6. Finally, z(t)=u(x_0+t(x−x_0)) solves the same ODE as v with z(1)=v(1). Hence z=v, and so u(x_0)=y_0.

The page ends with a methodological remark. One could go on to the homogeneous form of Frobenius (exterior algebra, local primitives of closed holomorphic exterior forms), but perhaps that should wait for the chapter on analytic manifolds. This is the classical proof found, e.g., in Dieudonné's Foundations of Modern Analysis (10.9). The page reads like a draft or referee-style comment on a text on analytic geometry, misfiled or reused (backside) among the 1965 motives notes.
errors: No mathematical error. Differentiating dv_j/dt = Σ_i (x_i−x_{i0}) U_{ij}(x_0+t(x−x_0);v) with respect to x_k and subtracting the displayed derivative indeed gives (27), via (24).
Minor gap: the proof silently uses differentiability of v with respect to the parameter x. This is standard ODE dependence on parameters and presumably established earlier.
The step 'z(t)=v(t)' could be seen directly, since v(1;x_0,x_0+t(x−x_0),y_0)=v(t;x_0,x,y_0) by rescaling. The uniqueness argument used is also valid.

ideas.what: Proof of the Frobenius integrability theorem (non-homogeneous form) by integrating along rays from x_0 and showing that the defect satisfies a linear homogeneous ODE vanishing at t=0
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius theorem for completely integrable Pfaffian systems (radial-ODE proof)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Frobenius (1877), Clebsch, Deahna; this proof is standard (e.g. Dieudonné, Foundations of Modern Analysis, 10.9)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA; the proof appears in Dieudonné's Éléments d'analyse

ideas.what: Remark about passing to the homogeneous (exterior-differential-system) form and local primitives of closed holomorphic forms, deferred to a chapter on analytic manifolds
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius theorem for distributions / holomorphic Poincaré lemma

deep.surprise_reason: Textbook proof of the Frobenius theorem in a typed course draft, unrelated to the motives material around it. Nothing new.
transcription_corrections: Transcription is essentially correct. In the second line of the derivative formula the image's summation is Σ_i, and in the third line and in (27) it is Σ_{i,h}; these are rendered correctly.
The final display reads z'(t)=U(x_0+t(x−x_0); z(t))·(x−x_0), with U underlined (matrix notation).
